issues.legal_issue: A written defense that expressly claims prescriptive ownership and alleges long, continuous possession raises a specific plea of adverse possession, even if the plea lacks material particulars needed to prove it.
material_facts: The written defense alleged that the defendant’s wife had been in continuous and peaceful possession since the alleged sale and expressly claimed that she had acquired ownership by adverse possession.
The High Court held that there was no specific plea, but the Supreme Court found that the written defense did contain one.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s finding that there was no specific plea of adverse possession could not be sustained; the written defense did specifically raise that plea, although it lacked material particulars necessary to establish it.
issues.legal_principle: A court must assess whether adverse possession has been pleaded from the contents of the written defense. An express claim of prescriptive ownership, read with allegations of long possession, is a specific plea; the sufficiency of the pleading does not establish the claim on its merits.

predicates.civil_appeal_from_possession_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree concerning possession of property.
predicates.written_defense_expressly_claims_prescri: The defending party expressly claims that possession has matured into ownership by prescription.
predicates.written_defense_alleges_long_possession: The written defense alleges long-term possession of the property.

issues.definition: When a defense in an appeal concerning possession expressly claims prescriptive ownership and alleges long-term possession, the adverse-possession plea is specifically pleaded.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot claim title under a transaction and simultaneously claim adverse possession from the same commencement of possession without renouncing the title-based claim and establishing when possession became hostile.
material_facts: The defendant’s wife was said to have entered possession under an alleged sale agreement in 1976, and the defense claimed both ownership under documents relating to that transaction and adverse possession from the same period.
The alleged sale agreement and related documents were not proved, and the defense did not establish when possession became hostile to the owner.
issues.conclusion: The claims of title under the alleged transaction and adverse possession from the same date were incompatible; adverse possession could not be recognized from that date without proof of when possession became hostile.
issues.legal_principle: Karnataka Board of Wakf v. Government of India states that title and adverse possession are mutually inconsistent and that adverse possession does not begin until the title-based claim is renounced. Mohan Lal v. Mirza Abdul Gaffar likewise requires a person who entered under an agreement to disclaim that right and prove an independent hostile assertion to the knowledge of the owner or successor. P.T. Munichikkanna Reddy v. Revamma and Ram Nagina Rai v. Deo Kumar Rai support the need to identify when the owner was dispossessed and when possession became adverse.

rule.if: civil_appeal_from_possession_decree and claimant_asserts_transaction_based_title and claimant_asserts_adverse_possession_from_same_entry and hostile_possession_start_not_established

predicates.civil_appeal_from_possession_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree concerning possession of property.
predicates.claimant_asserts_transaction_based_title: The claimant relies on a transaction as the basis for title to the property.
predicates.claimant_asserts_adverse_possession_from: The claimant also alleges that adverse possession began when possession was taken under that transaction.
predicates.hostile_possession_start_not_established: The claimant has not established when possession became hostile to the true owner.

issues.definition: When a claimant in a possession appeal relies on a transaction for title and also claims adverse possession from the same entry without establishing when possession became hostile, adverse possession cannot be counted from that entry.

issues.legal_issue: Adverse possession is not established unless the claimant proves possession that is open, peaceful, continuous and hostile to the true owner, identifies when it became hostile, and supports the claim with cogent evidence.
material_facts: The alleged adverse possessor was not examined at trial.
The alleged possession was said to have arisen from consideration paid under a sale agreement, but that agreement and related documents were found unreliable and were not proved.
The defense did not establish the date on which possession became hostile to the true owner.
The courts found serious discrepancies and alterations in the documents relied on to support the defense.
issues.conclusion: The claim of adverse possession was not proved, and the appellants failed to establish that the defendant’s wife had perfected title by adverse possession.
issues.legal_principle: Karnataka Board of Wakf v. Government of India requires possession to be nec vi, nec clam, nec precario: adequate in continuity, publicity and extent, and adverse to the true owner. P.T. Munichikkanna Reddy v. Revamma and M. Siddiq v. Mahant Suresh Das emphasize the need to establish the starting point of adverse possession. Ram Nagina Rai v. Deo Kumar Rai requires a party to plead and prove when permissive possession became adverse. The claim must have a clear and cogent basis because it defeats the true owner’s rights.

rule.if: civil_appeal_from_possession_decree and claimant_relies_on_adverse_possession and alleged_adverse_possessor_not_examined and hostile_possession_start_not_established and supporting_documents_unproved

predicates.civil_appeal_from_possession_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree concerning possession of property.
predicates.claimant_relies_on_adverse_possession: The defending party relies on adverse possession to resist the owner’s claim to possession.
predicates.alleged_adverse_possessor_not_examined: The person alleged to have acquired title by adverse possession is not examined in support of that claim.
predicates.hostile_possession_start_not_established: The claimant has not established when possession became hostile to the true owner.
predicates.supporting_documents_unproved: Documents relied on to support the claimed basis of possession have not been proved.

issues.definition: In a possession appeal, a claimant who relies on adverse possession does not establish it when the alleged possessor is not examined, the hostile start of possession is not established, and the supporting documents are unproved.

issues.legal_issue: A claim of title based on disputed sale and authority documents fails when the documents are unreliable and the alleged legal bar to registration is not proved.
material_facts: The defendant’s wife claimed title under an alleged sale agreement, a power of attorney and an affidavit.
Both courts found material discrepancies and alterations in those documents, including altered seals and signatures, and found the evidence of the alleged scribe unreliable.
The asserted prohibition on registering the sale was not supported by evidence.
The High Court affirmed the trial court’s findings on the documents, and the Supreme Court found no reason to disturb those concurrent findings.
issues.conclusion: The defendant’s wife did not establish title under the alleged transaction or the related documents.
issues.legal_principle: The party relying on documents to establish title bears the burden of proving them. The Supreme Court declined to disturb the concurrent factual findings that the documents were unreliable and unproved.

rule.if: civil_appeal_from_possession_decree and title_claim_depends_on_disputed_documents and disputed_documents_found_unreliable and asserted_registration_bar_unproved

predicates.civil_appeal_from_possession_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree concerning possession of property.
predicates.title_claim_depends_on_disputed_document: The claimant relies on disputed documents as the basis for title.
predicates.disputed_documents_found_unreliable: The courts find material discrepancies or alterations that make the relied-on documents unreliable.
predicates.asserted_registration_bar_unproved: The claimant does not prove the alleged legal bar that is offered to explain why the claimed transfer was not registered.

issues.definition: A document-based title claim in a possession appeal is not established when the relied-on documents are found unreliable and the asserted reason for non-registration is unproved.
